title: Page Links Open
eyebrow: Fix proposal · #329, a page link in a reply must open

short.lead: Today the page checkpoint counts any reply that contains ".html" as linking a page. It never checks whether the app can open that file. The app opens files only inside the session's folder. A file outside it either does nothing when clicked, or opens in the browser pane as a snapshot with scripts off, and a make_page.py page then shows an empty card. Both outcomes happened today with the docs map page. The fix makes the checkpoint check the path.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what it covers.
items: _PAGE_LINK_RE in hook.py (line 7299 on main) matches a claude.ai artifact link, a markdown picture, or the text ".html" anywhere in the reply. Three places use it: the long-reply note, the page checkpoint and the owed-page counter. The QA page link check in _record_qa_link matches the page's file name alone, so a link to a copy in another folder also counts.
Reused: every caller moves to one new function.
make_page.py writes into the current folder

By default it writes to docs/plans/ under the folder it runs in (make_page.py line 401 on main), so a page built normally is inside the session's folder. A page lands outside only when --project or --out points elsewhere, or when the page is moved by hand, which is what happened with the docs map page today.
A link counts only if it opens

A new function, _reply_links_page, replaces the bare pattern. An artifact link or a picture still counts. An .html link counts only when its path, resolved against the session's folder, is inside that folder. A reply whose only .html links point outside does not count, and the note says to copy the page into the session folder.

changes: new
_reply_links_page(reply, cwd) in hook.py
One function that says whether a reply links a page aj can open.

It finds each .html path in markdown links, file:/// links and bare paths, resolves relative ones against cwd, and accepts the reply if any one resolves inside cwd. A bare file name with no folder, such as "page.html" in a sentence, still counts, as it does today, so ordinary replies are not newly flagged.

The page checkpoint, the long-reply note, the owed-page counter and the QA link check
All four call the new function instead of the pattern.
Any ".html" in the reply counts; the QA check matches the file name alone.
Only a link that resolves inside the session's folder counts.
This fixes the cause once, in the place every caller already routes through.

Names the outside path and the fix.

make_page.py build

Silent.
"make_page: <out> is outside <cwd>; a link to it will not open in the app. Copy it into <cwd>/docs/plans/ before linking."
One print. The build itself is unchanged.
new
verify.py cases
Five cases for _reply_links_page and one for the make_page.py warning.

A link inside the folder counts; a ../sibling link does not; a file:/// link outside does not; an artifact link counts; a bare file name counts. The warning case builds into a temporary folder outside the current one and checks the printed line.

wrapup.summary: The page checkpoint stops counting links the app cannot open, and the page builder warns when it writes outside the session's folder.
wrapup.changing: hook.py (one new function, four callers), make_page.py (one warning), verify.py (six cases), the hook-engine doc and the version.
wrapup.next: A builder helper makes the change on a new branch off main, verify.py runs twice, and you get a QA page that opens.
